paragraphs: ZOLL makes medical devices, software and related services for patients with serious cardiopulmonary and respiratory conditions. Its buyers include hospitals and other healthcare organizations, emergency medical services and militaries.

One part of the catalog covers acute cardiac care, from sudden cardiac death protection to heart failure management and care after a heart attack. Another covers diagnostics meant to widen access to sleep apnea testing. There is also ventilation technology for patients from neonates to adults. The Zenix monitor/defibrillator is offered for EMS and hospital use. The history page records the launch of RescueNet, described as an EMS information management system covering patient care, operational efficiency and agency compliance. A subsidiary was later renamed ZOLL Data Systems to better reflect the EMS market.

The company traces its origins to Dr. Paul Zoll, a physician who co-founded it in 1980. The history page lists the co-founders as Dr. Zoll, Leigh Stein and Thomas Claflin. Its policy for interactions with health care professionals is based on the Advanced Medical Technology Association Code of Ethics. The company also certifies a compliance program satisfying the requirements of the California Health and Safety Code. Under the Sunshine Act it tracks payments and other transfers of value and reports them annually.

quote.text: ZOLL's mission is to improve patient outcomes and help save lives.
